findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the out-of-dir signing consumers (`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`: ensure_opcert_key/opcert_principal/mint_opcert_record/sign_opcert_manifest; `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`: sign_completion_verdict) and specify how the context-local signer/principal replaces their `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`/`REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` env reads.
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:169 `override = os.environ.get("REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH")`
src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:193 `override = os.environ.get("REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID")`

src/rebar/opcert_service/jobs.py:114-116 imports and calls transition_close.sign_completion_verdict, whose docstring states 'The service points REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH / REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID at the provisioned environment key before calling this'
src/rebar/opcert_service/keyprov.py:37-39 sets REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH / REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID in os.environ — the exact env seam the signer consumes
findings.finding: Step 3's move to a context-local signer/principal requires editing the signing producer seam that currently reads REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH / REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID from os.environ — src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py (ensure_opcert_key, opcert_principal, mint_opcert_record/sign_opcert_manifest) and src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:sign_completion_verdict — but the plan names none of these consumers outside opcert_service/.
findings.location: Plan step 3 ("passed through jobs/workspace/signing") / Acceptance Criteria bullet 3
scenarios: Job worker signs a PASS via sign_completion_verdict → sign_manifest → ensure_opcert_key, which still reads process env even after keyprov's env patching is removed
review_plan's internal signing path uses the same _opcert_signing env seam
findings.suggested_fix: Add the signing seam to the edit set: thread the immutable signer (key path/handle) and principal as explicit parameters through sign_completion_verdict → sign_manifest → mint_opcert_record / sign_opcert_manifest / ensure_opcert_key / opcert_principal, and state that the close-gate caller of the same seam retains its existing env/genesis behavior (or is likewise updated).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete durable-IaC edits for cutover: remove REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM/AWS_REGION/AWS_DEFAULT_REGION from the opcert compose service, declare the tmpfs-backed process-owned runtime directory in compose, and update infra/terraform/opcert-plan-assertions.sh and tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py to the new file/value contract.
evidence: Plan step 4: 'Update compose/Dockerfile/deployment bootstrap so SSM-at-rest may be materialized/mounted before process startup, but the application container receives the file/value contract and no SSM parameter/region permission for key retrieval.'
docker-compose.yml:269 REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM and :273-274 AWS_REGION/AWS_DEFAULT_REGION set on the opcert service
tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py:174 asserts env['REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM'] == '/rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key'
search: 'tmpfs' returns no matches under infra/ — the ADR-required ephemeral tmpfs backing of the runtime dir is not yet in the compose IaC
findings.finding: The plan states the compose/Dockerfile/deployment bootstrap change so SSM-at-rest is materialized/mounted before startup and the app container receives 'no SSM parameter/region permission for key retrieval', but it does not name the concrete durable-IaC edits this requires in lockstep — removing REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM / AWS_REGION / AWS_DEFAULT_REGION from the opcert compose service (docker-compose.yml lines 269–274), declaring the process-owned runtime directory's tmpfs backing (no tmpfs mount exists in the compose file today), and updating the deployment drift/assertion checks (infra/terraform/opcert-plan-assertions.sh, tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py which asserts REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM == '/rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key'). Leaving these implicit risks the compose service still carrying the SSM/region env after cutover and the drift sweep/deploy-infra tests reddening against the removed contract.
scenarios: Post-cutover the opcert compose service still exports REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM/AWS_REGION, contradicting AC4's 'no SSM/boto3/region/key-parameter dependency'
The runtime directory is not tmpfs-backed on the box, so a crash leaves the 0600 key copy on disk contrary to ADR 0098's 'kill/restart cannot retain the copy'
terraform-drift / deploy-infra tests keep asserting the removed SSM env var and go red

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item '[operator-attested] Hosted signing/restart/tmpfs canaries pass with the required' is [operator-attested] but its provenance declaration is incomplete (environment is missing (no provenance declaration found); principal is missing (no provenance declaration found); privilege_posture is missing (no provenance declaration found); instrument is missing (no provenance declaration found); justification is missing (no provenance declaration found)); add an indented continuation line 'provenance: environment=<v>; principal=<v>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <justification>' under the checkbox.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name in the plan how the deep resolution sites (ensure_opcert_key / opcert_principal / _store push-mode) consult the new context-local binding (contextvar read vs. explicit parameter) and state the ordering invariant (binding established before the first signing/push read, torn down after), confirming the shared close-gate producer seam is unaffected.
evidence: ensure_opcert_key reads os.environ.get('REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH') at src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:169; opcert_principal reads REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID at :193; _push_mode resolves REBAR_SYNC_PUSH via config at src/rebar/_store/push.py:40 — all below the opcert_service layer, inside the shared producer seam also used by the close gate (transition_close.sign_completion_verdict)
Plan step 3 says 'through jobs/workspace/signing' but does not state whether the chokepoints read a contextvar or take an explicit parameter
Absence rationale: the mechanism's correctness (no leftover global read winning over the context-local, binding set-before-read / torn-down-after) hinges on this unstated substitution
findings.finding: The plan commits to passing the signer/principal/push binding 'through jobs/workspace/signing' but does not name how the deep os.environ read-sites that actually resolve these values (ensure_opcert_key, opcert_principal, _push_mode) are converted to consult the context-local binding, nor the ordering guarantee that the binding is established before those reads fire and torn down after — the load-bearing correctness detail of the cutover.
findings.location: Plan step 3 / Outcome ('pass signer/principal/push policy context-locally to jobs')
scenarios: A signing path reached from a code branch that still falls through to the os.environ read wins over the new context-local, silently reintroducing global coupling
The close-gate producer (shared seam) is inadvertently altered because the binding is threaded as a parameter through mint_opcert_record

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly which source kind requires a mode check and the exact rejected mode threshold (e.g. path-source must be 0600/0400, else reject; value-source has no mode check).
evidence: 'Reject missing, both-set, unreadable, non-regular, wrong-mode where required, malformed, encrypted/passphrase, or non-Ed25519 input before service work.'
'where required' does not state the predicate (which source kind / which mode threshold triggers rejection)
findings.finding: The invalid-source case 'wrong-mode where required' is conditionally scoped without stating which sources require the mode check, leaving a defaultable ambiguity for the executor.
scenarios: Executor cannot tell whether REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH must be 0600 or merely readable, so the wrong-mode rejection is implemented inconsistently with the filesystem test expectation
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify step 1: 'For the path source, reject any mode broader than 0600 (group/other readable); the inline value source has no filesystem mode.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a Plan step and a Testing entry describing the sentinel/redaction work that AC5 measures (typed non-loggable signer, repr/serialization suppression, and a test enumerating the ten named surfaces).
evidence: AC: 'Secret/key sentinels are absent from repr, serialization, argv, logs, exceptions, output, fingerprints, provenance, children, and persisted envelopes beyond the existing public signature.'
Plan steps describe validation, copy, context-local signer, deployment, ADR preservation — no explicit redaction/no-leak deliverable named
Testing section has no dedicated leak/redaction test asserting absence across the ten named surfaces
findings.finding: Acceptance Criterion 5 (secret/key sentinels absent from repr, serialization, argv, logs, exceptions, output, fingerprints, provenance, children, persisted envelopes) has no clearly described covering deliverable in the Plan steps; steps 1-3 cover source validation, copy semantics, and context-local passing but do not describe the redaction/non-leak work AC5 measures.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria bullet 5 vs Plan steps 1-5
scenarios: Executor implements startup binding but leaks key bytes in a signer __repr__ or exception traceback
AC5 cannot be proven because no step produced a redaction mechanism or a test enumerating the surfaces
findings.suggested_fix: Add step 6: 'Wrap signer/key in a non-loggable type whose repr/str/serialization emit a redacted sentinel; assert absence across repr, serialization, argv, logs, exceptions, output, fingerprints, provenance, children, and persisted envelopes.' and a matching Testing bullet.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge that `_opcert_signing.py`'s signer/principal seam is shared with the local close/sign path and specify that path's behavior is preserved (or in-scope) when the gate service switches to context-local binding.
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:152-198 ensure_opcert_key/opcert_principal are the general producer seam (used by rebar.signing.sign_manifest for ordinary close/sign, per test_opcert_producer_seam_8d8e.py and test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py), keyed off os.environ overrides
the REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH override in ensure_opcert_key is documented as the gate hand-off but the function is the single seam for ALL op-cert signing
findings.finding: _opcert_signing.py's env-driven key/principal seam is shared with the non-opcert-service close gate (mint_opcert_record / ensure_opcert_key are reached by the local close/sign path, not just the gate service), so the context-local rework has blast radius into a caller the plan does not acknowledge.
scenarios: A local `rebar close`/`rebar sign` (not the gate service) relies on the genesis/env behavior of ensure_opcert_key/opcert_principal; a context-local rework of the seam signature must preserve that path

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that the instance-role SSM read grant (rebar-gerrit-ssm-params-read, /rebar/prod/*) is intentionally unchanged because boot-time materialization still reads the opcert key SSM value, and only the application-runtime read is removed.
evidence: AC4: 'Application runtime has no SSM/boto3/region/key-parameter dependency; deployment may still materialize ADR 0049's SSM value before startup.'
infra/terraform/iam.tf:50-61 ssm_params_read grant is namespace-scoped to /rebar/prod/* and is shared by boot materialization of all rebar secrets — not the app runtime
opcert.tf:13-14 notes the opcert SSM slots are already covered by the existing rebar-gerrit-ssm-params-read grant, 'NO new IAM here'
findings.finding: The plan's structural test asserts the application package has no boto3/SSM/region dependency, but does not consider narrowing or documenting the instance-role SSM read grant now that the application runtime no longer reads /rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key. The shared rebar-gerrit-ssm-params-read grant (iam.tf, scoped to /rebar/prod/*) legitimately remains for boot-time materialization of the key and other secrets, but the plan should state that the least-privilege posture is deliberately unchanged (boot materialization still needs the read) so a reviewer does not read AC4 as implying an IAM-scope reduction that is neither made nor needed.
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer reads AC4 as requiring the instance-role SSM grant to drop the opcert key parameter and breaks boot-time materialization of the key
